title: Design and validation of an executable, rollback-aware NetOps benchmark for action-level scoring (preregistered)
research_question: Can a compact, public executable benchmark (topology + intent corpus + rollback-aware scoring) reproducibly measure action-level correctness and rollback safety for LLM-driven NetOps pipelines, and do baseline pipelines (unconstrained LLM, guarded generate→verify→repair, verifier-only gating) produce statistically separable failure and rollback-necessity rates on that benchmark?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H0: The benchmark cannot reproducibly differentiate pipeline safety; baseline pipelines produce indistinguishable rollback-necessity rates on the confirmatory set.

H1: The benchmark can reproducibly measure differences: the three baseline pipelines (unconstrained, guarded generate→verify→repair, verifier-only gating) will show statistically separable rollback-necessity rates on the preregistered confirmatory set (paired tasks).
H2: Rollback-penalty-adjusted scoring yields a different pipeline ranking than verifier-pass-only scoring with at least one pairwise rank inversion among the three baselines on the confirmatory set.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How sensitive are pipeline rankings to verifier fidelity (simulated false-positive/negative rates) when measured on the discovery set?
EQ2: Which intent categories (e.g., segmentation, BGP, ACL change) drive most irreversible-state occurrences under each pipeline?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic + seeded corpus of device-config intents and executable sandbox topologies (6 topologies of increasing complexity).
Action-level execution semantics limited to sandboxed device command emulation (no production device connection).
Evaluation limited to the protocols and command subsets modelled in the sandbox and verifier (documented per-topology).
model_scope: Hosted LLM API(s) only (single hosted-model family selected at execution time consistent with capability manifest).
No local GPU LLMs; all LLM calls via hosted API under manifest limits (≤10000 planned model calls).
Verifiers and emulators are deterministic CPU-executable open-source tools run locally in Docker.
transformation_scope: Deterministic command parsing and normalization (AST canonicalization).
Rollback-emulation semantics applied to sandbox state traces; action-impact and rollback-necessity scoring computed from state diffs.
primary_estimand: Paired difference in rollback-necessity rate per task between pipelines (probability that a pipeline's executed action sequence leads to a state requiring rollback-emulation).
secondary_estimands: Verifier-pass rate per pipeline (proportion of tasks that pass verifier before/after repair attempts).
Mean action-impact score per pipeline (continuous score measuring deviation from expected ground-truth state).
Ranking consistency (Spearman rho) between verifier-pass ranking and rollback-penalty-adjusted ranking.
sampling_plan: Total corpus = 360 intents evenly across 6 topologies (60 intents per topology). Confirmatory = 300 items (50 per topology). Discovery/development = 60 items (10 per topology) held out for calibration and verifier-fidelity checks. Paired within-task design: each confirmatory task is executed under all three pipelines under the same seed.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: detect an absolute paired difference of 0.10 (10 percentage points) between pipelines with 80% power, alpha=0.05. Analytic McNemar-style calculations and preregistered bootstrap simulations (10,000 resamples, deterministic seeds) indicate required paired N≈300 given baseline rollback rate ≈30%. Post-hoc achieved-power and sensitivity analyses will be reported; alternative baseline rates (20%,40%) will be used in sensitivity checks.
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks that fail for technical reasons after two automatic retries with the same seed (API outages, verifier/emulator crashes). Excluded tasks are removed from confirmatory analysis and enumerated with failure reasons.

Exclude tasks exhibiting execution nondeterminism: if the same seed+task produces non-reproducible pipeline outputs across independent runs, mark the task and exclude it from confirmatory hypothesis tests (reported).
Count LLM outputs rejected during parsing/normalization (unsupported commands) as verifier-failure for that attempt; such tasks excluded only if unrecoverable after allowed retries.

Automatically reject and record any generated sequence containing preregistered forbidden operations; these are treated as unsafe proposals and counted as pipeline failures rather than dataset exclusions.
missingness_plan: Technical failures: retry up to two times automatically (same seed). If still failing, task excluded from confirmatory analysis and listed with cause. Discovery-set runs may be repeated for calibration. All exclusions, retry counts, and affected task IDs are reported. Sensitivity analyses report results including and excluding flagged/excluded items.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of rollback-necessity rates between pipelines on confirmatory N=300 using paired-proportions test (exact McNemar or equivalent exact test) with Holm-Bonferroni correction for the three primary pairwise comparisons; report exact p-values. Compute bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, preregistered seeds) for rates and paired differences. Secondary analyses: paired comparisons for verifier-pass rates; compare action-impact scores using paired t-test if normal or Wilcoxon signed-rank otherwise; compute Spearman rho for ranking consistency. Report effect sizes, exact p-values, and bootstrap CIs. All random seeds, code, raw outputs, and hashes saved; analyses deterministic given artifacts and seeds.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory family: three pairwise comparisons (unconstrained vs guarded, unconstrained vs verifier-only, guarded vs verifier-only). Control familywise error using Holm-Bonferroni across these three tests. Secondary estimands and exploratory tests corrected with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 0.05 when reporting multiple secondary outcomes.
contamination_plan: Benchmark names: CNSM-rollback-bench-v1 (public seedable artifact); one exemplar public topology referenced (https://openalex.org/W4399629579). Risk factors: overfitting to public confirmatory set, leakage between discovery and confirmatory items, verifier design dominating observed differences. Detection procedures: hold out 60 discovery intents; publish SHA256 hashes of released files and CI scripts to verify structure; compute per-task randomization fingerprints (seed+task id) and detect mismatches. Item-flagging rules: reproducible output differences under same seed → mark 'execution nondeterminism' and exclude; discovery-set estimated verifier FP/FN >10% triggers sensitivity analyses rather than strong claims. Analysis treatment: contaminated/excluded items reported; primary analyses on preregistered confirmatory set excluding only documented unrecoverable technical failures or nondeterminism; sensitivity analyses include flagged items and simulated verifier-fidelity perturbations. Residual uncertainty: benchmark topologies and verifier cannot prove generalization to all production networks; verifier-induced bias may remain despite checks.
stopping_rule: Automatic per-task stopping: for a given task, stop retrying after two automatic retries (total attempts = 3) and mark as technical exclusion. Global stopping: halt confirmatory execution early and switch to economy fallback if cumulative model-call count would exceed the planned budget (scenario-recommended: 1800 calls) or if more than 10% of confirmatory items become excluded due to technical failures/nondeterminism; in that case record the event, report reduced effective N, and run predefined sensitivity analyses. Also stop and abort the run if persistent infrastructure failure prevents completion (deterministic failure modes logged).
planned_outputs: Preregistration document (this JSON and human-readable text).
CNSM-rollback-bench-v1 artifact: topology files, intent corpus (360 items), sandbox/emulator Docker images, verifier code, normalization scripts, and published SHA256 hashes.
Execution manifest and raw model outputs for each pipeline and task (logs, timestamps, seeds, hashes).
Statistical-results file: rates, paired-test outputs, bootstrap CIs, effect sizes, and multiplicity-corrected p-values.
Failure-analysis record and per-task exclusion list with reasons.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (five pages max) and BibTeX bibliography.
Compiled PDF of manuscript (≤5 pages) including Disclosure Statement.
Autonomous revision and validation logs (methodological, statistical, reference-integrity reviews).
Final-output hash manifest for all released artifacts.
